notes: types: the 22 type words as the site and the API spell them, lowercase and singular.
refusals: every reason a reader or a writer refuses by, in the order a parser checks them (no_world and bad_form are the writer's only).

format cases: address gives form (human or text), world (absent for the in-world text form), type and id (both absent for a world's own address), and optionally lens and moment; expect is the exact string a writer writes, or refuse the reason.

parse cases: text is the string as a reader receives it; expect is the reading (form, world, world_is_slug, type, id, lens, moment, canonical; type and id null for a world's own address), or refuse the reason. canonical is true when the string as received is exactly what a writer writes for that reading.
ids: any UUID version, in the hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12 form; read in either case of hex, always written lowercase.

prose cases: text is a line as a reader finds it and index where an address starts in it; expect gives the address (the slice of text from index that the address covers, where it ends in prose) and its reading (what the parse cases answer for that slice). The whole-string parser is unchanged: handed the line's tail whole it may refuse. Every prose case is ASCII up to the end of its address (one holds a combining mark where no address is found), so its index and its address are the same whether a language counts UTF-16 units or code points.

cases.claim: a slug in prose ends at the first character outside its alphabet; an upper-case first letter leaves an empty run, which is no slug, so no address

cases.claim: a slug is the whole run or nothing: my-world- (its alphabet holds the hyphen) is no slug, so no address, never cut back to my-world

cases.claim: a slug is the whole run or nothing: 41 letters are no slug, so no address, never cut back to the first 40

cases.name: slug-that-is-a-type-word-is-no-address
cases.claim: a run that is a type word is no slug (the site reserves every type word), so event before a full stop is no address

cases.name: slug-ends-at-its-alphabet-the-full-stop-is-prose
cases.claim: a slug in prose ends at the first character outside its alphabet: hyperion is the world's slug, and the full stop after it is prose

cases.name: slug-run-followed-by-an-upper-case-letter-is-no-address
cases.claim: a run followed by a letter is cut inside a word and is no address: mop is followed by P, so mopPetopia is no address, never the slug mop

cases.name: slug-run-followed-by-an-underscore-is-no-address
cases.claim: a run followed by an underscore is cut inside a word and is no address: hyper is followed by _, so hyper_ion is no address, never the slug hyper

cases.name: after-w-a-run-past-an-id-with-a-hyphen-is-a-slug
cases.claim: after /w/ the run is read whole: an id's 36 characters, a hyphen and an x are no id's form and a legal slug, so the address is that slug, where the site sends the click, never the id with the rest as prose

cases.name: after-w-a-run-past-an-id-with-letters-is-a-slug
cases.claim: after /w/ the run is read whole: an id's 36 characters run on by abc are no id's form and a legal slug of 39 characters, so the address is that slug

cases.name: after-w-an-id-in-upper-case-is-the-worlds-id
cases.claim: after /w/ a run that is exactly an id's form is the world's id, read in either case and taken lowercase; the run takes the upper-case hex letters, so it does not end at the first A

cases.name: after-w-an-upper-case-id-run-on-by-a-hyphen-is-no-address
cases.claim: after /w/ the run is read whole: an upper-case id run on by a hyphen and an x is no id's form and no legal slug, so no address

cases.name: after-w-an-id-followed-by-a-letter-is-no-address
cases.claim: after /w/ the run ends at G, outside its alphabet; a run followed by a letter is cut inside a word, so no address, though the run is an id's form

cases.name: after-w-an-id-followed-by-an-underscore-is-no-address
cases.claim: after /w/ a run followed by an underscore is cut inside a word, so no address, though the run is an id's form

cases.name: slug-run-followed-by-a-combining-mark-is-no-address
cases.claim: a run followed by a combining mark is cut inside a word: cafe and then U+0301, a decomposed cafe with its accent, is no address, never the slug cafe
